prompt: Write a Python function `parse_row(line: str) -> list[str]` that splits one CSV row into fields. Handle quoted fields containing commas, and doubled quotes as an escaped quote. Output only the function.

fixtures.check.py:
import re, pathlib
src = pathlib.Path('ANSWER.md').read_text()
src = re.sub(r'^```[a-zA-Z]*\n|```$', '', src.strip(), flags=re.M)
ns = {}
exec(src, ns)
f = ns['parse_row']
assert f('a,b,c') == ['a','b','c'], f('a,b,c')
assert f('a,"b,c",d') == ['a','b,c','d'], f('a,"b,c",d')
assert f('"he said ""hi""",x') == ['he said "hi"','x'], f('"he said ""hi""",x')
assert f('') == [''], f('')
print('ok')

prompt: Write a Python function `parse_row(line: str) -> list[str]` that splits one CSV row into fields. Handle quoted fields containing commas, doubled quotes as an escaped quote, and a trailing newline on the input. Output only the function.

fixtures.check.py:
import re, pathlib
src = pathlib.Path('ANSWER.md').read_text()
src = re.sub(r'^```[a-zA-Z]*\n|```$', '', src.strip(), flags=re.M)
ns = {}
exec(src, ns)
f = ns['parse_row']
assert f('a,b\n') == ['a','b'], f('a,b\n')
assert f('a,"b,c"\n') == ['a','b,c'], f('a,"b,c"\n')
assert f('"x""y",z') == ['x"y','z'], f('"x""y",z')
print('ok')
